title: No Man's Sky Survived a Flood Before It Ever Launched
hook: Two weeks after four people stole the show with No Man's Sky at the 2013 VGX awards, a flood wiped out Hello Games' office and insurance wouldn't cover it. Ten years and forty free updates later, the game just landed on iPhone. Which planet would you name first?

script: Did you know the studio behind No Man's Sky lost almost everything in a flood just two weeks after revealing the game? Hello Games was a tiny team in Guildford, England. Founder Sean Murray had left big budget studios to make games with three friends around a dining room table. Their first game was Joe Danger. Then on December seventh, two thousand thirteen, that four person team showed off No Man's Sky at the VGX awards and stole the show. On Christmas Eve a nearby river burst its banks and flooded their office. Computers, equipment and personal belongings were lost. The studio said its insurance would not cover it, because the office sat in a flood risk zone. They kept going anyway. No Man's Sky launched on PlayStation Four and PC in August of two thousand sixteen, with a universe of about eighteen quintillion planets. The launch was rough, but Hello Games never charged for an update. Ten years later it has released forty major updates, every one of them free. Sean Murray says players have still explored less than one percent of its planets. And this week the whole game landed on iPhone and iPad for the first time, in a download of about four gigabytes. Which planet would you name first? Follow for more gaming history.
